article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: DNA Cake × Challah Bread
Breeder: DNA Genetics
THC Content: 26%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: Myrcene dominant
Primary Flavors: Sweet baked goods, cream, vanilla, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: 450–570 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Heavy
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Challah Cake takes the modern dessert-strain idea in a direction that feels heavier, earthier, and more traditional than its name initially suggests. Sweet baked goods and cream form the first aromatic impression, but those softer notes quickly encounter Kush, damp earth, herbs, and a sharp diesel edge. DNA Genetics created the cultivar from DNA Cake × Challah Bread, combining one parent built around Gelato, Cookies, and Grape Pie-related dessert genetics with another rooted much more strongly in Kosher Kush and bakery-style sweetness. The result smells less like frosting alone and more like warm bread and cake sitting beside a container of pungent Kush.

Its cultivation profile is equally substantial. Plants grow with a sturdy, bushy indica structure, tolerate a variety of media, and complete flowering in approximately nine weeks. Dense resin production gives mature flowers a heavily frosted appearance, while breeder-listed yields of 16–20 ounces per square meter place the cultivar firmly in the productive category. The effects favor relaxation as the session develops, making Challah Cake particularly suited to consumers who want sweet modern marijuana without abandoning the deeper physical character associated with classic indica breeding.
Genetics and Lineage

DNA Genetics bred Challah Cake from DNA Cake and Challah Bread. DNA Cake itself comes from Gelato Sorbet × Lava Cake and contributes much of the creamy, sugary side of the cross. Gelato Sorbet combines Gelato #33 with Sorbet, tying the parent to the Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint Cookies family that helped define modern dessert cannabis. Lava Cake adds another Cookies family layer through Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies × Grape Pie , introducing dense resin, dark fruit, sweetness, and a heavier physical character.

Challah Bread brings a different form of dessert influence. DNA Genetics created it from Bakers Delight × Kosher Kush . Bakers Delight combines Cookies-derived genetics with the breeder’s Sorbet line, producing sweet baked-goods aromas and dense flower, while Kosher Kush contributes the deep earthy, pungent, and physically relaxing qualities for which it became famous. Kosher Kush also gives the parent a more traditional indica foundation than many modern cake strains possess, helping explain Challah Bread’s strong body effects and hardy structure.

The finished cross therefore contains several overlapping sources of cream, baked sweetness, resin, and Kush, but each parent emphasizes them differently. DNA Cake leans toward frosting, dessert cream, Gelato-style sweetness, and modern trichome-heavy flower, whereas Challah Bread contributes bread dough, earth, pungency, and heavier Kush depth. That combination prevents Challah Cake from becoming a one-note sugar strain and gives the flower a savory, diesel-backed foundation beneath the sweeter surface.
Effects and Experience

The experience usually begins with a noticeable but relatively calm cerebral shift. Mood can become lighter, thoughts less demanding, and ordinary entertainment more immersive without the rapid mental acceleration associated with highly stimulating sativas. There may be a short period of euphoria or increased sociability, but the cultivar’s indica dominance becomes increasingly apparent as the session develops. Music, movies, conversation, or a relaxed evening at home generally fit the early stage better than demanding work.

Physical heaviness builds progressively. Shoulders loosen, limbs begin to feel weighted, and the desire to remain active often fades as the high settles deeper into the body. Larger servings can produce pronounced couch-lock and eventual sleepiness, while moderate amounts may stop at a comfortable level of relaxation. That dose-sensitive progression gives the strain some flexibility, but its overall direction remains clear: the experience moves toward calm rather than sustained stimulation.

DNA Genetics does not attach one universal THC percentage to every Challah Cake plant, although the breeder positions the cultivar as potent and resin rich. Consumers with limited tolerance should therefore treat well-grown flower cautiously rather than judging strength by the smooth, creamy flavor. Dry mouth and dry eyes are possible, and excessive consumption may bring dizziness, mental haze, or an unexpectedly heavy sedative effect.
Medical Benefits

The cultivar may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer pronounced physical relaxation accompanied by a quieter mental state. As the body effect deepens, muscular tension and general physical discomfort may become less intrusive, while the calmer cerebral character can make it easier to disengage from stress. The strain’s overall profile makes it more naturally suited to evening use than situations requiring sustained attention, coordination, or rapid decision-making.

Heavier servings may increase appetite and drowsiness, which can make the later stages useful for consumers who prefer cannabis as part of a nighttime routine. Strong indica-style marijuana is not universally calming, however, and people who are especially sensitive to THC may still experience dizziness, anxiety, or uncomfortable mental heaviness after consuming too much. Gradual dosing remains more reliable than assuming the strain’s relaxing reputation guarantees the same response for everyone.

Myrcene is identified by DNA Genetics as the dominant terpene, matching the herbal and earthy side of the aroma. Other aromatic characteristics include cream, sweetness, Kush, and diesel, but exact terpene ratios can vary according to phenotype and cultivation. Medical use is best guided by cannabinoid and terpene testing from the specific harvest, along with personal tolerance, medications, and previous response to THC-rich cannabis.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Freshly baked sweetness is the most distinctive part of the bouquet. The flower can suggest warm bread, cake batter, vanilla cream, or lightly sweet dough before the deeper notes begin to emerge. That bakery character comes from both sides of the pedigree, but DNA Cake pushes it toward cream and frosting while Challah Bread gives it a warmer, more bread-like quality.

Breaking apart the buds reveals the heavier side of the cultivar. Earth, herbs, and Kush become much stronger, followed by diesel that adds a sharp contrast to the soft sweetness. Some phenotypes may remain creamier and more dessert oriented, while others emphasize pungent Kush and fuel. Myrcene helps give the aroma its earthy, comforting depth and keeps the strain from resembling a purely candy-focused hybrid.

On the palate, sweet cream and baked goods tend to arrive first, followed by earthy Kush and herbal notes through the middle of the inhale. Diesel often becomes more pronounced on the finish, leaving a pungent aftertaste beneath the lingering sweetness. Vaporization can preserve the cream and vanilla characteristics particularly well, while combustion usually gives greater weight to earth, fuel, and resin. A patient cure helps the different layers remain distinct instead of collapsing into generic sweetness.
Growing Information

Challah Cake develops a sturdy, bushy frame typical of indica-dominant cannabis. DNA Genetics describes the cultivar as adaptable to both soil and hydroponic cultivation, making it accessible to growers using very different setups. Plants can become dense with foliage, so strategic pruning helps open the center of the canopy and prevents shaded lower growth from consuming resources. Topping or low-stress training can also spread the main branches outward and create a wider productive surface beneath indoor lighting.

Flowering takes approximately nine weeks. DNA Genetics lists yields of 16–20 ounces per square meter, equivalent to roughly 450–570 g/m² under good conditions. Resin production becomes increasingly obvious as the flowers mature, and the compact buds benefit from strong light throughout bloom. Because the plants can become thick and leafy, humidity management is one of the most important environmental considerations. Continuous air movement and regular canopy maintenance help prevent moisture from remaining trapped around dense flowers.

Outdoor cultivation benefits from abundant direct sunlight and enough seasonal warmth to complete the nine-week flowering cycle. In many Northern Hemisphere climates, this places harvest around early to mid-October, although latitude and the natural onset of flowering can shift the schedule. The breeder does not provide one standardized outdoor yield figure, so final production depends on root volume, vegetative time, climate, irrigation, nutrition, and training. The plant’s sturdy nature and resin production make it a strong candidate for growers who want a forgiving dessert hybrid without sacrificing serious flower density.
FAQ
What strains make Challah Cake?
Challah Cake was bred by DNA Genetics from DNA Cake × Challah Bread. DNA Cake comes from Gelato Sorbet × Lava Cake, while Challah Bread combines Bakers Delight with Kosher Kush.
Is Challah Cake indica or sativa?

Challah Cake is an indica-dominant hybrid, commonly listed at approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa. Its bushy growth, dense flowers, and increasingly heavy physical effects all reflect the stronger indica influence.
What does Challah Cake taste like?
The primary flavors include sweet baked goods, cream, vanilla, earth, Kush, herbs, and diesel. The dessert-like beginning gradually gives way to a more pungent and savory finish.
How long does Challah Cake take to flower?

DNA Genetics lists an indoor flowering period of approximately nine weeks, or around 63 days. Outdoor maturity generally falls during autumn, often around early to mid-October in suitable Northern Hemisphere environments.
Is Challah Cake easy to grow?

Yes. DNA Genetics describes the cultivar as hardy and adaptable to both soil and hydroponic cultivation. Its main challenge is managing the dense bushy canopy and controlling humidity around resinous flowers late in bloom.
Final Thoughts on Challah Cake

Challah Cake succeeds because it treats dessert genetics as more than sweetness alone. DNA Cake brings Gelato, Cookies, Grape Pie, cream, and heavy resin into the cross, while Challah Bread contributes the earthy Kush depth and baked-dough personality of Bakers Delight and Kosher Kush. The finished cultivar moves between frosting and bread, sweetness and fuel, modern flower quality and traditional indica character.

Its cultivation traits make that flavor practical rather than merely exotic. A nine-week flowering period, breeder-listed production of roughly 450–570 g/m², sturdy branching, broad adaptability, and dense trichome development give growers substantial potential without requiring an unusually complicated routine. Maintaining airflow and controlling humidity are the primary concerns as the compact buds gain weight.

For consumers, this cannabis strain gradually reveals its identity. Sweet cream and bakery notes make the first impression, earthy Kush and diesel add depth, and the effects move from calm euphoria toward increasingly strong physical relaxation. Challah Cake is therefore more than another pastry-named marijuana hybrid: it combines modern dessert breeding with an unmistakable Kush backbone, producing a cultivar that feels both contemporary and reassuringly old-school.
